text:
I read this on Complex.

In the song’s opening bars, Kendrick seemingly mocks Drake for constantly rapping about rich shit that normal people can’t relate to (like going “from the Vava to Cinquante-Cinq, then back to the Vava”), but there could also be some hidden layers behind them. Drake recently purchased a new Rolls Royce Phantom, and this could be a double entendre, with Dot implying that he doesn’t have to move silently like a ghost (or in the same vehicle as Drake) and he’d rather make it very loud and clear that he’s pulling up on people. Cole and Drake also reunited in a Rolls Royce Ghost in 2019, which might have pissed Kendrick off. Drake also recently bought a yacht, so in the next line, Dot raps that he doesn’t need glamorous items because “money, morals, and culture” are enough to satisfy him, implying that Drake is filling these holes in his life with material possessions. Finally, Drake frequents Ibiza as a vacation spot, so Dot appears to be saying he’s not afraid to pull up on him anywhere.

OJ Simpson’s murder case began on June 16, 1995, and this reference could tie into the black leather glove on the song’s cover artwork, which might be Kendrick’s way of implying that some of Drake’s own crimes will soon come to light.

Fans are also pointing to the Bible verse, Corinthians 6:16, which reads, “Do you not know that he who unites himself with a prostitute is one with her in body? For it is said, ‘The two will become one flesh.’” This could be yet another jab at Drake’s tastes in women.

The song is built around a sample of Al Green’s “What a Wonderful Thing Love Is,” which has direct ties to Drake’s family. Drake’s father’s cousin, Mabon “Teenie” Hodges, was a guitarist and songwriter for Al Green, and he’s credited for playing on this specific song.

text:
I'm just going to drop a note about the number 3 in spirituality, since it's a very significant number in different religions and often represents the 3 parts that comprise 1 (God, wholeness, completion, etc). There's a passage in Revelation that stands out to me as possibly related or portending what's to come in this war, just as the 3 Revelation Angels did. In that passage, we see the Divine & Holy, the mouthpiece of God, speaking down to man (K to D).

We also see "3" throughout the entire Bible: Holy Trinity (Father, Son, Holy Spirit), the Evil Trinity (Satan, Antichrist, False Prophet), 3 Angels in Revelation (let's come back to this), Jesus's age at death (33), Jesus's resurrection after 3 days, the 3 Kings and 3 gifts, and much more. 

I don't know much about Kendrick's spiritual leaning, but I'd be interested in whether you think the 3 Angels of Revelation are relevant here especially since he mentioned "3 Angels watching over me" (Michael, Gabriel, Raphael) to represent what is holy and what is protected by the Holy (Kendrick, i.e. those who align w/ God). We see 3 Angels (unnamed) again in Revelation 14:6-13, right before Jesus appears, and each Angel has a warning: 1) humans should fear and worship God, 2) Babylon will fall, 3) anyone who engages in false worship will suffer God's wrath. 

One more big one -- Kendrick mentions 3 indirectly in the following lines, referring to Drake's entourage: "And 20 of them want you as a casualty, 1 of them is actually next to you, 2 of them is practically tired of your lifestyle." During the Last Supper, Jesus predicts that he'll be betrayed and denied 3 times by his Apostles before dawn (Matthew 26:34).
